messages.author: 6a288128bce8283d
messages.subject: unmarked occu WinBUGS comparison
parts:
Hello all!

I am trying to get the occupancy model to run in WinBUGS and noticed
that my results are very different from the occu function in unmarked.
Now I was wondering if there is something wrong with my WinBUGS model
specification. Here the model I use (modified version of Richard's
lecture example):

model {

## Priors

a0 ~ dunif(-10, 10)
aCR_CL_2 ~ dunif(-10, 10)
aOF_100 ~ dunif(-10, 10)
b0 ~ dunif(-10, 10)
bFOR2_1KM ~ dunif(-10, 10)

## Model

# State process
for(i in 1:630) {
logit(psi[i]) <- min(max(
a0
+aCR_CL_2 * CR_CL_2[i]
+aOF_100 * OF_100[i]
, -629), 629)
Z[i] ~ dbern(psi[i])

# Detection process
for(j in 1:12) {
logit(p[i, j]) <- b0
+bFOR2_1KM * FOR2_1KM[i]
y[i, j] ~ dbin(p[i, j], Z[i])
}
}
}

Running this model I get from R2WinBUGS

Iterations = 2001:4000
Thinning interval = 1
Number of chains = 2
Sample size per chain = 2000

1. Empirical mean and standard deviation for each variable,
plus standard error of the mean:

Mean SD Naive SE Time-series SE
a0 2.1883 0.96984 0.015335 0.096480
aCR_CL_2 2.6301 0.76822 0.012147 0.061159
aOF_100 1.3471 0.71412 0.011291 0.062022
b0 -1.1076 0.10838 0.001714 0.005887
bFOR2_1KM 0.0899 0.07355 0.001163 0.001430

The output from the occu function is:

Call:
occu(formula = ~FOR2_1KMZ ~ CR_CL_2Z + OF_100Z, data = UMF)

Occupancy:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
(Intercept) 1.55 0.697 2.23 0.025935
CR_CL_2Z 2.16 0.641 3.38 0.000734
OF_100Z 1.10 0.523 2.10 0.035984

Detection:
Estimate SE z P(>|z|)
(Intercept) -1.074 0.1113 -9.65 4.75e-22
FOR2_1KMZ 0.098 0.0734 1.33 1.82e-01

AIC: 956.582


Do I specify something incorrectly in the BUGS model here?

Another question I have regarding the BUGS model is: how do you
incorporate a categorical survey specific covariate into the model (I
have observer as a categorical covariate).

And one more question regarding the auto-logistic model I want to
eventually fit: would you set the a's and b's to a fixed value (that I
get from my occu model averaging runs) or would you let them be
recalculated as I did in the above model?

Thank you very much for your help,
Richard

messages.author: 681fb59733e01a1e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] unmarked occu WinBUGS comparison
parts:
hi Richard,
(1) I suggest trying first the model without covariates to make sure you get similar answers.
(2) Second, are the covariates standardized in both cases?
(3) the Bayesian posterior means will be a bit different but, with that sample size, I'm surprised that they're as different as you report. Thus, try (1) and (2) first.
regards
andy

messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: unmarked occu WinBUGS comparison
parts:
Hi Richard,

If you want to make sure that occu is working, I would try simulation. This is pretty compelling:

nSites <- 500
nReps <- 10
x1 <- rnorm(nSites)
x2 <- rnorm(nSites)
psi <- plogis(-1 + x1)
p <- plogis(0 + -x2)
Z <- rbinom(nSites, 1, psi)
y <- matrix(rbinom(nSites*nReps, 1, Z*p), nSites)

umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y, siteCovs=data.frame(x1=x1, x2=x2))
(fm <- occu(~x2 ~ x1, umf)) # estimates should be close to -1, 1, 0, -1


There are a lot of reasons why BUGS could give you different results. I don't think this list should be a place to discuss BUGS issues, but did you assess convergence? Did you try different priors? Did try to avoid the min/max trick?

You will need to create dummy variables if you want to use categorical variables. See ?model.matrix.

Richard

> p <- plogis(0 + -x2)
> Z <- rbinom(nSites, 1, psi)
> y <- matrix(rbinom(nSites*nReps, 1, Z*p), nSites)
>
> umf <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y, siteCovs=data.frame(x1=x1, x2=x2))
> (fm <- occu(~x2 ~ x1, umf)) # estimates should be close to -1, 1, 0, -1
>
> There are a lot of reasons why BUGS could give you different results. I
> don't think this list should be a place to discuss BUGS issues, but did you
> assess convergence? Did you try different priors? Did try to avoid the
> min/max trick?
>
> You will need to create dummy variables if you want to use categorical
> variables. See ?model.matrix.
